docs.title: Philter AI Proxy
docs.text:
Philter AI Proxy is a self-hosted proxy for OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google Gemini (public API and Vertex AI), Ollama, Amazon Bedrock, and OpenAI-compatible providers. It removes PII, PHI, and other sensitive information from LLM requests before they leave your network, and can scan the responses on the way back. Streaming and non-streaming requests are supported.

Redaction runs inside the proxy with Phileas, the library under Philter. Policies are standard Phileas policies, so a policy works the same in the proxy and in Philter, except that the proxy refuses policies that name a PhEye service, generators, or files and environment variables the deployment has not allowed; see What a policy may not do. The proxy needs no other service: person names are detected with a PhEye model that ships in the Docker image and runs in-process.

docs.title: How it Works
docs.text:
The proxy receives the request an application would send to the provider, redacts the text in it according to a policy, and forwards the redacted request with the application's own provider credentials (for Vertex AI, Amazon Bedrock, and Azure OpenAI with Entra ID, the proxy authenticates with its own). For example, the request text How old is George Washington? reaches the provider as How old is {{{REDACTED-name}}}?.

  • Inbound redaction covers the text of every message, including system prompts, content parts, refusals, and tool-call arguments and results. See Redacted Fields.
  • Outbound scanning, turned on per route, scans the provider's response before it reaches the application: redact what it finds, block the response, or pass it through and record what was found. Streamed responses are scanned as they arrive. See Response Scanning.
  • Policies are managed through an admin API with the paths of Philter's policy API, under /admin. See Policies.
  • Consistent pseudonymization: a context keeps the replacement chosen for a value, so the same value is replaced the same way across requests. See Contexts.
  • An audit log records each request's metadata (provider, model, policy, how many values of each type were found), never the text of a prompt or response. See Monitoring.

Detection is probabilistic: the proxy reduces how much sensitive data reaches a provider, and it does not catch every instance. Validate its output against your own data and policies.

docs.title: Deployment options
docs.text:
• Docker: the philterd/philter-ai-proxy image, with the person-name model included. See Installation.
  • From source: build with Maven and run the jar on Java 25. See Installation.

The proxy keeps its policies, API keys, contexts, and audit log in a SQLite file, so one instance serves each database file. See FAQ.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
The proxy does redaction and the audit trail that goes with it. It deliberately does not do routing, failover, token quotas, or per-tenant billing; those belong to an AI gateway, and the proxy is designed to run alongside one. See Using with an AI Gateway.

It also handles text conversations only. The proxy accepts JSON request bodies and does not parse multipart/form-data, so file uploads, audio, and image edits are rejected with 400 invalid_request / unsupported_content_type. Audio support is tracked in #40; image edits and file uploads are not planned. See Supported request types.

Only text is redacted. A JSON request carrying images, audio, video, or files (such as image and audio content parts) is refused by default, or forwarded with the media unchanged and uninspected when media is set to forward. Media in responses is returned unscanned. See Images, audio, and files are not redacted.

docs.title: Using with an AI Gateway
docs.text:
Philter AI Proxy is a redaction proxy. It does not do routing, failover, model fallback, rate limiting, response caching, token quotas, spend tracking, or per-tenant billing. Those are the job of an AI gateway such as LiteLLM, Portkey, Kong AI Gateway, or a cloud provider's own gateway.

The two are complementary. Run the gateway for traffic management and the proxy for redaction.

docs.title: Recommended topology
docs.text:
Put the proxy between the gateway and the provider, so redaction is the last thing that happens before data leaves your network:

client -> AI gateway -> Philter AI Proxy -> LLM provider
                              |
                              +-> audit log

This ordering matters. Anything downstream of redaction cannot undo it, and no gateway plugin, retry path, or model-fallback rule can route around it. If the gateway is instead placed after the proxy, a fallback to a provider the proxy did not see, or a gateway-injected system prompt, can put unredacted text on the wire.

Configuration on the gateway is two changes: point its upstream base URL at the proxy instead of at the provider, and send a proxy key in the x-philter-proxy-key header. The proxy speaks each provider's native wire protocol, so the gateway needs nothing else. Create a key with the proxy role for the gateway; see API keys.

docs.title: LiteLLM
docs.text:
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-4
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4
      api_base: https://philter-ai-proxy.internal:8080/v1
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
      extra_headers:
        x-philter-proxy-key: pap_your-proxy-key

docs.title: Portkey
docs.text:
Set the provider's custom host on the virtual key or in the request config, and have Portkey send the x-philter-proxy-key header to it:

{
  "provider": "openai",
  "custom_host": "https://philter-ai-proxy.internal:8080/v1"
}

docs.title: Kong AI Gateway
docs.text:
Override the upstream on the ai-proxy plugin:

plugins:
  - name: ai-proxy
    config:
      route_type: llm/v1/chat
      model:
        provider: openai
        options:
          upstream_url: https://philter-ai-proxy.internal:8080/v1/chat/completions
  - name: request-transformer
    config:
      add:
        headers:
          - "x-philter-proxy-key:${PHILTER_AI_PROXY_KEY}"

docs.title: Behind a gateway
docs.text:
When the gateway is the trust boundary and the proxy is on a private network reachable only by the gateway:

Proxy feature Behind a gateway Proxy keys Always required. One key for the gateway is enough; give it a policy to pin every request to one policy, or use separate keys per team to give each its own policy and scopes. proxy.limits.max-concurrent-requests Keep. This protects the proxy from overload regardless of what sits in front. Audit log Keep. This is the record of what was redacted, and no gateway produces it. proxy.security.trusted-proxies Set it to the gateway's addresses if the gateway passes on its clients' addresses in X-Forwarded-For, so the audit log records them.

See Configuration.

docs.title: When you do not need the proxy
docs.text:
If your gateway supports guardrail callbacks (LiteLLM, Portkey, and Kong all do), it can call Philter, Philterd's redaction API, directly, and you can skip the proxy entirely. That is a legitimate setup and it is simpler when it fits.

The proxy is the better choice when you want redaction enforced at the network layer rather than as a feature of the gateway's configuration:

  • It cannot be toggled per request. A guardrail hook is a gateway config that a developer with gateway access can disable, reorder, or bypass with a direct call. A proxy in the network path cannot be routed around.
  • It covers traffic the gateway does not. Applications that call providers directly, SDKs pinned to a provider base URL, and anything that predates the gateway can be pointed at the proxy without touching the gateway.
  • It is the last hop. Redaction happens after every gateway decision has been made, including retries and fallbacks.

For a compliance boundary you have to defend to an auditor, the network-layer version is easier to demonstrate. For convenience redaction inside an already-governed gateway, the callback is fine.

docs.title: Token accounting
docs.text:
The proxy does not track token usage at all: not in the audit log, not as a metric. Token counts say nothing about redaction, and duplicating them here would mean carrying per-provider usage-parsing for every provider and streaming format the proxy supports, to produce a partial copy of what the gateway already records accurately.

Use the gateway's accounting as the system of record for spend, budgets, and per-tenant usage. If you run without a gateway, the provider's own usage dashboard is the source of truth.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: The proxy serves two APIs on port 8080: provider traffic, which it redacts and forwards, and the admin API under /admin, for policies and API keys. See Usage for which path goes to which provider.

docs.title: Redacted Fields
docs.text:
The proxy redacts the text-bearing fields of each request before forwarding it. Every other field, such as model names, sampling parameters, tool definitions, and IDs, is forwarded unchanged.

Provider Request Fields redacted OpenAI family Chat completions Each message's content (a string, or the text or refusal of each content part), refusal, reasoning_content and reasoning (OpenAI-compatible servers), tool_calls[].function.arguments, and function_call.arguments; prediction.content OpenAI family Responses (/responses) instructions; prompt.variables (strings and input_text values); input as a string, or each item: message content (a string or input_text and output_text parts), function_call.arguments, function_call_output.output (a string or input_text parts), custom tool call input and output, mcp_call arguments, output, and error, shell call output (including stdout and stderr), and reasoning summaries and text OpenAI family Embeddings, moderations, speech (/audio/speech) input (a string or an array of strings; token-ID arrays are left alone) OpenAI family Image generation, legacy completions prompt (a string or an array of strings); suffix (legacy completions) Anthropic Messages (/v1/messages, /v1/messages/count_tokens), and each request's params in a message batch (/v1/messages/batches) system (a string or text blocks); each message's content (a string, or text blocks, tool_use input, search_result titles and text, and tool_result content as a string, text blocks, or search results); the citations of text blocks sent back from earlier turns (cited_text and the source's title) Gemini, Vertex AI generateContent, streamGenerateContent, countTokens Each part's text, functionCall.args, functionResponse.response, executableCode.code, and codeExecutionResult.output, in contents and systemInstruction; for countTokens, also in a wrapped generateContentRequest, and every string in Vertex AI's instances Gemini embedContent, batchEmbedContents The parts of content, as above, and title, in the request or in each of requests Ollama /api/generate prompt, system, suffix, template Ollama /api/chat Each message's content, thinking, and tool_calls[].function.arguments Ollama /api/embed, /api/embeddings input (a string or an array of strings); prompt (/api/embeddings) Ollama /api/show Nothing: the request names a model, and neither it nor the response carries conversation text. Forwarded unchanged Bedrock Converse system[].text and guardContent text; each message's text blocks, guardContent text, toolUse.input, and toolResult.content (text and JSON) Bedrock InvokeModel, Anthropic Claude models The Messages API fields listed for Anthropic above, and prompt for legacy Text Completions models (Claude 2, Instant). With response scanning on, a legacy model's stream cannot be scanned and is ended with response_unscannable, except under flag, where it is forwarded unscanned Bedrock InvokeModel, Amazon Titan embedding models inputText Bedrock InvokeModel, Cohere Embed models texts, and the text parts of inputs

The OpenAI family is OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, and the OpenAI-compatible providers. Arguments and other JSON held in a string are parsed, each string in them redacted, and the JSON written back when something in it changed; when they are not valid JSON, or repeat a name within an object, the whole string is redacted as text.

Not redacted: Anthropic thinking blocks and Bedrock reasoning blocks sent back in a conversation. The providers verify their signatures, so a redacted block would make the request fail. Their text reaches the provider as the client sends it. If thinking can hold sensitive values, have the client drop thinking blocks from the conversation history it sends back.

Embeddings are computed from the redacted text. Search by meaning still works on such embeddings, but a search for a redacted value matches any text where that kind of value was redacted, not that value. When documents and queries are redacted with the same policy and context, and the policy's strategy replaces a value the same way each time, an exact value can still be matched through its replacement. The client's own copy of the text is not changed.

All the fields of one request are redacted together, against one policy. Without a configured context, a value is replaced the same way in every field of the request and in its response, when the policy's strategy uses "replacementScope": "CONTEXT". See Contexts.

docs.title: Images, audio, and files are not redacted
docs.text:
Only text is redacted. The proxy does not inspect images, audio, video, or files embedded in a JSON request, including any text, faces, or spoken words they contain. By default it refuses a request that carries one with 400 invalid_request / media_not_allowed, and the error message names the part it found. Set media: forward in proxy.defaults or on a route to forward such requests instead, with the media unchanged. See Routes.

Provider Parts refused, or forwarded unredacted under media: forward OpenAI / OpenAI-compatible / Azure OpenAI Chat completions: every content part other than text, input_text, output_text, and refusal, such as image_url, input_audio, file, or an OpenAI-compatible server's video_url. Responses API: input_image, input_file, input_audio, and computer_screenshot, in messages, tool outputs, and prompt.variables. Moderations: image inputs Anthropic image, document, and container_upload content blocks, including those in tool results and message batches Gemini / Vertex AI inlineData and fileData parts, including those in function responses, a wrapped generateContentRequest, and embedding requests Bedrock Converse image, document, and video content blocks, including those in tool results, and images in guardContent (system or message) Bedrock InvokeModel Claude: as for Anthropic. Titan: inputImage. Cohere Embed: a non-empty images list, and inputs parts other than text Ollama A non-empty images list

The same holds for responses: response scanning reads response text only, so generated images and audio, and the transcript that accompanies audio output, are returned unscanned. media applies to requests only.

If images, audio, or files sent to a provider can contain sensitive data, remove or redact them before the request reaches the proxy, or route those requests elsewhere. Multipart uploads (files, audio transcription, image edits) are refused under either setting; see Supported request types.

docs.title: Supported request types
docs.text:
The proxy accepts a JSON request body. It does not parse multipart/form-data. It decodes the request path once (so /v1/chat/completion%73 is handled as /v1/chat/completions) and forwards the path as the client encoded it.

Request type Behavior Error The requests in the table above Redacted, then forwarded - A request without a body, such as GET /v1/models Forwarded unchanged when response scanning is off for its route. With scanning on, refused unless the endpoint is in the table above, since its response cannot be scanned. To a provider the proxy authenticates to with its own credential (Vertex AI, Bedrock, and Azure OpenAI with Entra ID), refused unless the endpoint is in the table above, since the proxy would otherwise act for any key on any endpoint, such as deleting resources 400 invalid_request / unsupported_endpoint Any other request with a JSON body, such as /v1/batches, /v1/threads/{id}/messages, Anthropic /v1/messages/batches/{id}/cancel, or Vertex AI :predict Refused by default: the proxy does not know where the text is, so it cannot redact it. Set unsupported-endpoints: forward on a route to forward it unredacted, with its response unscanned 400 invalid_request / unsupported_endpoint /v1/images/edits, /v1/images/variations Refused. Not supported, and not planned 400 invalid_request / unsupported_content_type /v1/files (uploads) Refused. Not supported, and not planned 400 invalid_request / unsupported_content_type /v1/audio/transcriptions, /v1/audio/translations Refused today. Support is tracked in #40 400 invalid_request / unsupported_content_type A JSON request carrying images, audio, video, or files Refused, unless media is forward for the route 400 invalid_request / media_not_allowed A body that is not a JSON object, or not strictly valid JSON (RFC 8259: no single quotes, unquoted names, comments, trailing commas, or raw control characters in strings), or that repeats a name within an object Refused 400 invalid_request / bad_json

Route refused calls directly to the provider.

Why image edits are not planned. Redacting the prompt form field would mean parsing a multipart body, rewriting one field, and re-encoding the rest, which the proxy deliberately does not do.

Why file uploads are not planned. A batch file is many embedded requests, so redacting one upload would mean redacting every record inside a single synchronous request. Redact the file contents before uploading.

Why audio can be supported. Audio needs no multipart parsing: the body is binary with no inbound text to redact, so it can be forwarded untouched and the transcript scanned on the way back.

docs.title: Endpoints by provider
docs.text:
A request with a body to an endpoint not listed as redacted is refused with unsupported_endpoint unless unsupported-endpoints is forward. Uploads (multipart/form-data) are refused with unsupported_content_type under either setting. The refused column names common examples, not every endpoint. A request without a body, such as listing models, retrieving a batch's results, or cancelling a batch or response, is forwarded unchanged when response scanning is off, except to the providers the proxy authenticates to itself (Vertex AI, Bedrock, and Azure OpenAI with Entra ID), where it is refused.

Provider Redacted Refused (examples) OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible Chat completions, Responses, legacy completions, embeddings, moderations, image generation, speech Creating batches, file uploads, Assistants and threads, vector stores, fine-tuning, updating a stored chat completion, audio transcription and translation, image edits and variations. The Realtime API (WebSocket) is not proxied Anthropic Messages, token counting, creating a message batch Files API uploads Gemini, Vertex AI :generateContent, :streamGenerateContent, :countTokens; on Gemini, also :embedContent and :batchEmbedContents Vertex AI embeddings (:predict, :embedContent) and other :predict calls, cached contents, file uploads. The Live API (WebSocket) is not proxied Amazon Bedrock Converse and ConverseStream for any model. InvokeModel for Anthropic Claude, Amazon Titan embedding, and Cohere Embed models, and InvokeModelWithResponseStream for Claude, by model ID or cross-region inference profile ID (such as us.anthropic.claude-...) InvokeModel for other model families, such as Meta Llama, Mistral, and Amazon Nova; ApplyGuardrail; asynchronous invocation. A model given as an ARN is refused with 400 under either setting, since its / is sent encoded as %2F, which is not accepted in a path Ollama /api/generate, /api/chat, /api/embed, /api/embeddings; /api/show is forwarded unchanged /api/create, /api/copy, /api/pull, /api/push, /api/delete. Pull and delete can be forwarded with routes; see Model management

docs.title: Response Scanning (Outbound)
docs.text:
By default, provider responses are returned unchanged. When a route turns on outbound scanning (Configuration), the proxy scans the response with the route's policy before returning it.

Provider Response fields scanned OpenAI family, chat Each choice's message content (a string or text parts), refusal, reasoning_content and reasoning, and tool-call and function-call arguments OpenAI family, Responses Each output item, read as the request's input items are: message text and refusals, function and custom tool call arguments and input, tool and MCP call output, and reasoning summaries and text OpenAI family, legacy completions Each choice's text OpenAI family, image generation Each image's revised_prompt Anthropic text blocks and their citations (the quoted cited_text and the source's title), tool_use and server_tool_use input, and thinking text Gemini, Vertex AI Each candidate's text parts (including thought summaries), function-call arguments, and executable code and its output; and its grounding metadata: the answer passages citations quote, the search and retrieval queries, the rendered search suggestions, the titles and text of grounding sources (web, image, Google Maps places and their review titles, and documents retrieved from Vertex AI Search, a file search store with its string metadata, or the Vertex AI RAG Engine), and the content of generateAnswer's grounding attributions. Citation offsets into the answer are not adjusted, so once the answer is redacted they are approximate Ollama response and thinking, or the message's content, thinking, and tool-call arguments Bedrock, Converse output.message.content: text, toolUse.input, and reasoning text Bedrock, InvokeModel (Claude) As for Anthropic, and a legacy model's completion

Redacting an Anthropic thinking block invalidates its signature, so a client that sends the redacted block back in a later request is refused by Anthropic. Bedrock reasoning blocks behave the same way.

Responses from other OpenAI endpoints, such as embeddings and moderations, from Ollama's embeddings and /api/show, from Gemini and Vertex AI countTokens and Gemini embeddings, and from Bedrock's Titan and Cohere embedding models, carry no generated text and are returned unchanged. Audio, image, and video bodies are returned unchanged.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Action Normal response Streamed response redact (default) Values found are replaced, and the response returned Values found are replaced as the text is released block 403 pii_blocked / outbound_blocked instead of the response The stream ends with an error event before the text containing the value is sent flag Returned unchanged; the values found are counted in the audit log and logged as a warning Released unchanged; the values found are counted in the audit log

Under redact and block, data that spells out the original text and cannot be redacted to match is removed: OpenAI logprobs (set to null, or an empty array in the Responses API), Gemini logprobsResult and the search entry point's sdkBlob (the search terms, base64-encoded), Ollama logprobs and context (the conversation's token IDs), and Bedrock guardrail traces (trace in Converse, amazon-bedrock-trace in InvokeModel), which can quote the text a guardrail matched.

In JSON such as tool-call arguments, strings are redacted, and so are integers of five or more digits, since an SSN, phone number, or account number can be sent as a number. A number the policy changes is replaced by its redacted text, as a string. Shorter integers, decimals, and object keys are not redacted.

A response that cannot be scanned is refused rather than returned unscanned: one that arrives compressed (the proxy asks for an uncompressed response), one that is not strictly valid JSON or repeats a name within an object, a stream from an endpoint the proxy cannot scan (for example embeddings), a binary response (audio/, image/, video/, application/octet-stream) from any endpoint but speech, a redirect or other 1xx or 3xx status, a stream event whose name is not a plain identifier, and a Bedrock stream that carries an exception message get 502 provider_error / response_unscannable. A response larger than proxy.limits.max-response-body-bytes, or a stream with a line, event, or held text over 16 Mi characters, gets response_too_large. A provider's error responses (status 400 and above) are returned unchanged and unscanned. In a scanned stream, an event without data (a keep-alive comment, or only id: or retry: lines) is forwarded as a bare : comment, and id: and retry: lines are dropped from events with data, since their text is not scanned. A stream the provider cuts short is ended with an error event and recorded in the audit log as stream_interrupted.

docs.title: Streamed responses
docs.text:
The proxy scans a stream as it arrives instead of forwarding each fragment at once:

  • Text is held back. Once twice the holdback has accumulated (proxy.streaming.holdback-characters, default 256), the held text is scanned and all but the last holdback characters are released, cut at whitespace and never inside a detected value. A value split across fragments is scanned whole as long as it is shorter than the holdback.
  • What is left is released when its part of the response finishes (a choice, a content block, a candidate) and when the stream ends.
  • Tool-call arguments are held whole until their part finishes, then scanned and sent in one fragment. The fragment that opens a tool call (its ID and name) is sent at once.
  • Keep-alive comments and pings are forwarded at once.
  • Released text is sent in events shaped like the provider's own. In the Responses API, a released delta repeats the sequence_number of the delta it was copied from.
  • Under block, the stream has already started with 200, so a detection ends it with an error event in the stream's own format, such as data: {"error": {"type": "pii_blocked", "code": "outbound_blocked", ...}}. A Bedrock stream is ended with an AWS event stream error message (:message-type error, with the code in :error-code), which AWS SDKs raise. A stream holding data that is not a valid event is ended the same way, with response_unscannable, except under flag. A stream is also ended this way with response_too_large, or with redaction_failed when scanning fails.

Holding text back delays each fragment by up to two holdbacks of text. A smaller holdback releases text sooner and catches only shorter values split across fragments.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The proxy's own errors on provider traffic use the shape OpenAI-compatible clients parse. type and code are stable; message may change.

{"error": {"message": "missing API key", "type": "unauthorized", "code": "missing_api_key", "request_id": "6f1c..."}}

Every response carries an X-Request-Id header, which the audit log records. An inbound X-Request-Id of at most 128 printable ASCII characters is kept; any other is replaced with a new ID.

Status type code Meaning 400 invalid_request path_not_canonical The path is not in canonical form once decoded (.., empty segments), or has an escape that decodes to invalid UTF-8, a control character, or one of %, ?, #. A malformed escape or an encoded / or \ (%2F, %5C) is refused with a plain 400 from the web server, without this body 400 invalid_request ambiguous_field An OpenAI-family or Ollama request names a field the proxy reads (such as a redacted field, model, or name) in another case, such as Messages or Model, or with ſ or K (Kelvin sign), which Go's encoding/json folds to s and k. A server that ignores case would read it in place of the field the proxy checked. Keys inside tool definitions, schemas, metadata, and tool arguments are not checked 400 invalid_request unsupported_endpoint The endpoint is not one the proxy can redact, or, with response scanning on, scan; and unsupported-endpoints is reject. See Supported request types 400 invalid_request unsupported_content_type The body is multipart/form-data 400 invalid_request bad_json The body is not a JSON object, is not strictly valid JSON, or repeats a name within an object 400 invalid_request media_not_allowed The request carries an image, audio, video, or file part and media is reject. See Images, audio, and files are not redacted 401 unauthorized missing_api_key, invalid_api_key No proxy key, or an unknown one 403 forbidden scope_denied_role The key lacks the proxy role 403 forbidden scope_denied_provider, scope_denied_model, scope_denied_path The request is outside the key's scopes 403 pii_blocked outbound_blocked Response scanning under block found a value 404 not_found azure_disabled, vertex_disabled, bedrock_disabled, ... The path's provider is not configured 403 forbidden vertex_project_denied A Vertex AI path (/v1/projects/... or /v1beta1/projects/...) names a project or location other than the configured one 413 payload_too_large request_body_too_large The body is larger than proxy.limits.max-request-body-bytes 502 provider_error response_too_large Response scanning is on and the response is larger than the proxy will scan. See Response Scanning 500 configuration_error policy_not_found, policy_invalid The route's policy does not exist, or cannot be used (for example, it names a model that is not installed). A request without a body whose response is not scanned does not use the policy, so it is forwarded 500 redaction_error redaction_failed Redaction failed; the request was not forwarded 500 internal_error internal_error An unexpected failure in the proxy; the log has the details under the request ID 502 provider_error unreachable The provider could not be reached 502 provider_error <provider>_auth_failed The proxy could not get its own credentials for Bedrock, Vertex AI, or Azure (Entra ID) 502 provider_error response_unscannable Response scanning could not read the response 503 redaction_error redaction_timeout Redaction took longer than proxy.limits.redaction-timeout-ms 503 capacity concurrency_exceeded proxy.limits.max-concurrent-requests was reached; retry after Retry-After

When redaction fails, the request is not forwarded.

For requests routed to Bedrock, the error code is also sent in the x-amzn-ErrorType header, and the body carries a top-level message ("<code>: <message>"), so AWS SDKs report them.

docs.title: Admin API
docs.text:
The admin API manages policies and API keys. Every call needs a key with the admin role as Authorization: Bearer <key>; the bootstrap key has it. Errors use the shape of Philter's API:

{"message": "The policy changed since it was read. Read it again and retry.", "reason": "policy_changed"}

reason is stable; field names the invalid parameter, field, or header (If-Match) when there is one. Reasons: invalid_request (400), invalid_credentials (401), missing_scope (403, the key lacks the admin role), not_found (404), policy_exists, policy_changed, policy_default, and self_action_refused (409), and internal_error (500). Every response carries an X-Request-Id header, recorded with the audit events the call causes.

A request with a body needs Content-Type: application/json. A request under /admin, or to /livez, /readyz, or /health, that no endpoint accepts (an unknown path, or the wrong method or content type) is answered 404 not_found and never forwarded to a provider.

docs.title: Policies
docs.text:
The policy endpoints have the paths and bodies of Philter's policy API, under /admin. A client that takes a Philter base URL, such as philter-sdk-java, can use https://<proxy>/admin. Bodies are native Phileas policy JSON; see Policies.

Method and path Does GET /admin/api/policies?offset=0&limit=25 Lists policies by name: {"policies": [{"name", "revision", "description", "createdAt", "updatedAt"}], "total"}. limit is 1 to 500. POST /admin/api/policies?name=<name> Creates a policy. 201, with an ETag. 409 policy_exists when the name is taken. GET /admin/api/policies/<name> The policy JSON, with an ETag. PUT /admin/api/policies/<name> Replaces the policy and increments its revision. 200, with the new ETag; 404 when the policy does not exist. With If-Match: <ETag>, the write happens only if the policy has not changed since that read, else 409 policy_changed. Without If-Match, or with *, the write is unconditional. DELETE /admin/api/policies/<name> Deletes the policy. 204. The default policy cannot be deleted (409 policy_default).

A policy is checked when it is saved and again before it is used, and refused with 400 and the reason when it is not valid or names something the deployment does not allow. A name cannot contain /, \, ;, %, or control characters, cannot be . or .., and is at most 256 characters.

docs.title: API keys
docs.text:
Method and path Does POST /admin/api/keys Creates a key. 201, with the key's fields and the key itself in key, shown only this once. GET /admin/api/keys Lists keys, without their secrets: {"keys": [{"id", "name", "createdAt", "roles", "providers", "models", "paths", "policy"}], "total"}. policy is present only when one is bound. DELETE /admin/api/keys/<id> Deletes a key. 204; 404 when there is no such key. A key cannot delete itself (409 self_action_refused).

The create body:

{
  "name": "support-bot",
  "roles": ["proxy"],
  "providers": ["openai", "anthropic"],
  "models": ["gpt-4o*", "claude-*"],
  "paths": ["/v1/chat/completions", "/v1/messages"],
  "policy": "support"
}
Field Meaning name A label for the key, at most 256 characters. Required. roles admin (the admin API), proxy (provider traffic), or both. Required. providers Providers the key may reach. Empty: any. An entry ending in * matches by prefix. models Models the key may request. Empty: any. An entry ending in * matches by prefix. A request that names no model is refused when this is set, and so is one whose body names models other than its own: an Anthropic message batch whose requests name different models, or a Gemini countTokens or batchEmbedContents request naming a model other than the one in its path. paths Paths the key may use. Each covers itself and the paths below it, on a segment boundary: /v1/messages allows /v1/messages/count_tokens but not /v1/messagesx, and a Gemini model path allows its methods (...:generateContent). Paths are matched after decoding, against the path as sent, so an OpenAI-compatible provider's paths include its prefix (/vllm/v1/chat/completions). Empty: any. policy A policy applied to every request with this key, whatever the route says. It must exist.

Keys are 32 random bytes, prefixed pap_ so secret scanners can recognize them, and stored as SHA-256 hashes. A deleted key stops working on the instance at once.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Two credentials are involved in every request, and they are separate:

  1. A proxy key authenticates the client to the proxy. The proxy checks it, applies the key's roles and scopes, and never forwards it.
  2. A provider credential authenticates the request to the LLM provider. Depending on the provider, it is the client's own key, passed through, or a credential the proxy holds for the whole deployment.

A proxy key never translates into a provider credential. The proxy has no user accounts: API keys are its only identities.

docs.title: Proxy keys
docs.text:
Every request to a provider needs a proxy key in the x-philter-proxy-key header (configurable with proxy.security.proxy-key-header). A request without one is refused with 401 missing_api_key, and one with an unknown key with 401 invalid_api_key. There is no anonymous access.

Keys are created and deleted through the admin API. Each key has:

  • A name, such as support-bot. The audit log records the key's ID with each request, and with each admin action (creating or deleting a key or policy).
  • Roles. proxy allows provider traffic; admin allows the admin API. A key can hold both, but separate keys are easier to scope and to rotate.
  • Scopes (optional) on the providers, models, and paths the key may use. A request outside them is refused with 403.
  • A bound policy (optional), applied to every request with the key. A key with a bound policy also skips routes that match on a header, so its client cannot choose a route that forwards media or turns off response scanning. See Routes.

Keys created through the admin API are 32 random bytes, prefixed pap_. Every key, including the bootstrap key, is stored only as a SHA-256 hash. A key is shown once, when it is created. A deleted key stops working at once.

The admin API takes its key as Authorization: Bearer <key>, as Philter's clients send it, and needs the admin role.

docs.title: The first key
docs.text: On first start, while no key exists, the proxy creates an admin key from proxy.security.bootstrap-api-key (PHILTER_AI_PROXY_BOOTSTRAP_API_KEY, at least 32 characters). The key's secret is the configured value itself, and the key is named bootstrap. Use it to create the keys your applications use. It is created only while the database holds no key. A shorter value stops the proxy at startup; with no value, the proxy starts without a key and logs a warning.

docs.title: Unauthenticated endpoints
docs.text: /livez, /readyz, and /health on port 8080 answer without a key, for probes and load balancers. The metrics port (9090) is also unauthenticated; keep it off the internet.

docs.title: Provider credentials
docs.text:
Provider Credential sent to the provider OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible providers The client's own: Authorization, x-api-key, x-goog-api-key, or Gemini's ?key=, forwarded unchanged Azure OpenAI The client's api-key or Authorization, forwarded unchanged. With entra-id: true, the proxy's Entra ID token instead Vertex AI The proxy's Google application default credentials, replacing any Authorization the client sends Amazon Bedrock The proxy's AWS credentials (SigV4, optionally assuming role-arn). No client credentials are forwarded; of the client's headers, only X-Amzn-Bedrock-* settings are

When client headers are forwarded, the proxy removes the proxy key header, every header starting with x-philter-, hop-by-hop headers, Accept-Encoding (so the response can be scanned), X-Request-Id, X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto, and Forwarded.

docs.title: Passed-through credentials
docs.text:
For the providers in the first two rows, the proxy stores no provider secrets. Each application sends its own provider key alongside its proxy key:

curl -k https://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "x-philter-proxy-key: $PROXY_KEY" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}'

The proxy key decides whether the request is allowed and which policy applies; the provider key decides which provider account is used. The proxy does not choose or restrict the provider account.

docs.title: The proxy's own credentials
docs.text: For Azure with Entra ID, Vertex AI, and Bedrock, the proxy uses one credential, configured for the deployment (see Providers). Every key that may reach the provider uses it, so a proxy key alone grants access to the provider through that credential. Use the key's providers and models scopes to decide which clients may use it. A Vertex AI path that names a project or location other than the configured one is refused. With unsupported-endpoints: reject, the default, the credential is used only for the endpoints the proxy redacts: a request to any other endpoint of these providers is refused, with or without a body. A route with unsupported-endpoints: forward lets every key that matches it use the credential on that path.

docs.title: Keeping provider keys out of applications
docs.text: The proxy cannot hold a provider key and add it for a client. If applications must not see provider keys, put an AI gateway that maps its own keys to provider credentials (such as LiteLLM or Portkey virtual keys) behind the proxy. See Using with an AI Gateway.

docs.title: Mutual TLS
docs.text: The proxy can also require a client certificate signed by a CA you name, in addition to the proxy key. See Certificates.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Give each application its own proxy key, scoped to the providers, models, and paths it uses, so a leaked key reaches only that and can be deleted alone.
  • Bind a policy to keys whose clients must not choose their route.
  • Keep admin keys with administrators, one per person, so the audit log shows who made a change, and never in an application.
  • Scope keys carefully for providers the proxy authenticates to itself (Azure with Entra ID, Vertex AI, Bedrock), since the key is the only credential the client needs.

docs.title: How settings are given
docs.text:
The proxy is a Spring Boot application. Its settings come from, in increasing precedence:

  1. The defaults in the image's application.yaml.
  2. A file of your own, loaded with SPRING_CONFIG_ADDITIONAL_LOCATION=file:/path/to/application.yaml.
  3. Environment variables.
  4. Command-line options, such as --proxy.defaults.policy=support.

An environment variable's name is the setting's name in capitals, with . and [] as _ and hyphens removed: proxy.providers.openai.target is PROXY_PROVIDERS_OPENAI_TARGET, proxy.security.trusted-proxies is PROXY_SECURITY_TRUSTEDPROXIES, and proxy.routes[0].match.model is PROXY_ROUTES_0_MATCH_MODEL.

Two settings also have shorter environment variables, used in the examples:

Variable Setting PHILTER_AI_PROXY_ENCRYPTION_KEY proxy.security.encryption-key PHILTER_AI_PROXY_BOOTSTRAP_API_KEY proxy.security.bootstrap-api-key

--validate-config checks the settings without serving requests; see Installation.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
proxy:
  providers:
    bedrock:
      region: us-east-1
    openai-compatible:
      vllm:
        target: http://vllm.internal:8000
  defaults:
    policy: default
  routes:
    # Scan responses for one model and keep replacements consistent across requests.
    - match:
        model: gpt-4o
      context: support-conversations
      outbound:
        enabled: true
        action: redact
    # A stricter policy for one team, chosen by a header their gateway sets.
    - match:
        header: x-team
        value: finance
      policy: finance
  limits:
    max-concurrent-requests: 200
  security:
    trusted-proxies:
      - 10.0.0.0/8

docs.title: Security and storage
docs.text: Setting Default Meaning proxy.security.encryption-key (required) Encrypts values stored at rest: policies, and each context's replacements. 32 random bytes as 64 hex characters or base64: openssl rand -hex 32. The proxy refuses to start with a key other than the one its database was created with. proxy.security.bootstrap-api-key An admin key created on first start, while no API key exists. At least 32 characters. proxy.security.proxy-key-header x-philter-proxy-key The request header that carries the proxy key on provider traffic. It is never forwarded. proxy.security.trusted-proxies none Load balancers and proxies (IP addresses or CIDR ranges) whose X-Forwarded-For is believed for the client address in the audit log. The header is read from the right, skipping trusted proxies. proxy.storage.sqlite-path /var/lib/philter-ai-proxy/philter-ai-proxy.db The SQLite database: policies, API keys, contexts, and the audit log. Created readable only by the proxy's user. One instance per file. proxy.audit.file A file each audit entry is also appended to, as one JSON line. See Audit log. proxy.audit.retention-days 0 (kept) Entries older than this are deleted from the database, once a day. Standard output and the audit file are not pruned.

docs.title: Policies and models
docs.text: Setting Default Meaning proxy.models.directory /opt/philter-ai-proxy/models Local PhEye models, one per subdirectory. See Models. proxy.policy-files.directories none Directories the files a policy names (such as dictionary files) must be inside. With none, a policy may name no file. proxy.policy-files.allowed-environment-variables none Environment variables a policy may name as env:NAME, such as a key for CRYPTO_REPLACE. With none, a policy may name none.

docs.title: Defaults and routes
docs.text: Setting Default Meaning proxy.defaults.policy default The policy for a request no route matches. proxy.defaults.context none The context for a request no route matches. See Contexts. proxy.defaults.outbound.enabled false Whether responses to requests no route matches are scanned. proxy.defaults.outbound.action redact redact, block, or flag. See Actions. proxy.defaults.unsupported-endpoints reject reject refuses a request with a body to an endpoint the proxy cannot redact; when response scanning is on, a request to an endpoint whose response it cannot scan; and any request to such an endpoint of a provider the proxy authenticates to itself (Vertex AI, Bedrock, and Azure OpenAI with Entra ID). forward sends such requests on unredacted, with responses unscanned. See Supported request types. proxy.defaults.media reject reject refuses a request carrying images, audio, video, or files, which the proxy does not redact; forward sends it on with the media unchanged. See Images, audio, and files are not redacted. proxy.routes none Routes, in order; see Routes.

docs.title: Limits and streaming
docs.text: Setting Default Meaning proxy.limits.max-request-body-bytes 10485760 (10 MiB) Larger request bodies are refused with 413. proxy.limits.max-concurrent-requests 200 Requests handled at once; more are refused with 503 and Retry-After: 1. A negative value removes the limit. proxy.limits.redaction-timeout-ms 30000 How long redacting one request, or scanning one response or stream window, may take. A request that takes longer is refused with 503 redaction_timeout; a stream is ended with an error. proxy.limits.max-response-body-bytes 33554432 (32 MiB) The largest response read to scan it. A larger one is refused with 502 response_too_large. Applies only when response scanning is on; streams are bounded per line, event, and held text instead. proxy.streaming.holdback-characters 256 How much of a streamed response is held back so a value split across fragments is scanned whole. See Streamed responses.

docs.title: Server and TLS
docs.text:
Setting Default Meaning server.port 8080 Provider traffic and the admin API. management.server.port 9090 Prometheus metrics at /metrics, always plain HTTP. proxy.tls.dev-self-signed-cert true in the image, false otherwise Serve HTTPS with a self-signed certificate generated at startup. Configured key material (server.ssl.certificate, server.ssl.key-store, or server.ssl.bundle) takes precedence. server.ssl.certificate, server.ssl.certificate-private-key Your certificate and key in PEM form, to serve HTTPS. server.ssl.enabled-protocols Limit the TLS versions, such as TLSv1.3,TLSv1.2. Any server.ssl setting turns TLS on, so set it together with a certificate and key. server.ssl.trust-certificate, server.ssl.client-auth For mutual TLS: the PEM file of the CA that signs client certificates, and need. server.tomcat.connection-timeout 10s How long the proxy waits for a request to start, and between reads of it. Not a deadline for the whole request, so a client that sends a byte at a time can hold a connection; a load balancer in front of the proxy absorbs slow clients. server.max-http-request-header-size 1MB Larger request headers are refused.

The proxy does not limit how many TLS handshakes run at once. Put a load balancer or ingress in front of it to absorb a flood of handshakes or connections.

See Monitoring for the tracing settings.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text:
Provider Setting Enabled OpenAI proxy.providers.openai By default, at https://api.openai.com Anthropic proxy.providers.anthropic By default, at https://api.anthropic.com Gemini proxy.providers.gemini By default, at https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com Ollama proxy.providers.ollama By default, at http://localhost:11434 Azure OpenAI proxy.providers.azure When target is set Vertex AI proxy.providers.vertex When project is set Amazon Bedrock proxy.providers.bedrock When region is set OpenAI-compatible proxy.providers.openai-compatible.<name> For each name with a target

Every provider takes:

Field Default Meaning target as above The provider's base URL. connect-timeout-ms 5000 How long to wait to connect. response-timeout-ms 120000 How long to wait for the response to begin. A stream may then run as long as it lasts. ca-cert A PEM file of certificate authorities to trust for this provider instead of the system's, such as for a self-hosted server with a private CA. disabled false Turns off a provider that is on by default. A request for it is refused with 404.

Redirects from providers are not followed.

docs.title: Azure OpenAI
docs.text:
proxy:
  providers:
    azure:
      target: https://my-resource.openai.azure.com
      api-version: 2024-10-21
      entra-id: false

api-version is added to requests that do not send one. With entra-id: true, the proxy authenticates with an Entra ID token from the default Azure credential chain (managed identity, workload identity, environment variables, and so on) instead of passing the client's api-key through.

docs.title: Vertex AI
docs.text:
proxy:
  providers:
    vertex:
      project: my-project
      location: us-central1

Requests go to https://<location>-aiplatform.googleapis.com unless target is set; with neither location nor target, the proxy does not start. A request whose path names another project, or another location when location is set, is refused with 403 vertex_project_denied, since the proxy's credential is used for it. The proxy authenticates with Google application default credentials (a service account key named in GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, workload identity, or the metadata server), replacing any Authorization the client sends.

docs.title: Amazon Bedrock
docs.text:
proxy:
  providers:
    bedrock:
      region: us-east-1
      role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/philter-ai-proxy

Requests go to https://bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com unless target is set. The proxy signs each request with SigV4, with credentials from the AWS default chain (environment variables, a profile, web identity, or instance and container roles), assuming role-arn when it is set. Only Content-Type, the client's X-Amzn-Bedrock-* headers (guardrail, trace, latency tier, and service tier settings), and the signature are forwarded; the client's other headers are not.

docs.title: OpenAI-compatible providers
docs.text:
proxy:
  providers:
    openai-compatible:
      vllm:
        target: http://vllm.internal:8000
      mistral:
        target: https://api.mistral.ai

Each is reached at /<name>/v1/... and redacted like OpenAI. A name is lowercase letters, digits, -, and _, and cannot be one the proxy's own paths use (v1, v1beta, api, openai, model, admin).

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
A route chooses the policy, context, and response scanning for the requests it matches. The first route whose every set condition matches applies; a request no route matches uses proxy.defaults.

Field Meaning match.path The request path, exactly, after any OpenAI-compatible prefix is removed. match.model The model the request names, exactly. match.header, match.value A request header and the value it must have. policy The policy to apply. Without one, proxy.defaults.policy. context The context to keep replacements in. Without one, proxy.defaults.context. outbound.enabled, outbound.action Response scanning for the route. A route without outbound does not scan responses. media reject or forward for requests carrying images, audio, video, or files. Without one, proxy.defaults.media. unsupported-endpoints reject or forward for requests the proxy cannot redact or scan. Without one, proxy.defaults.unsupported-endpoints. Pair forward with match.path to allow one endpoint.

A key created with a policy overrides the route's policy. See Choosing the policy for a request.

proxy:
  routes:
    - match:
        path: /v1/embeddings
      policy: embeddings
    - match:
        header: x-scan-responses
        value: "true"
      outbound:
        enabled: true
        action: block
    - match:
        model: gpt-4o
        header: x-team
        value: vision
      media: forward
    - match:
        path: /v1/batches
      unsupported-endpoints: forward

A header match is only as trustworthy as whoever sets the header. When clients can set it themselves, they can choose their route, including one that forwards media or turns off response scanning. A key with a bound policy skips every route that matches on a header: its requests use only routes that match on path and model, then proxy.defaults. Bind a policy to the keys of clients that must not choose.

docs.title: What is the Philter AI Proxy?
docs.text: A self-hosted proxy for LLM providers that removes PII, PHI, and other sensitive information from requests before they leave your network, and can scan responses on the way back. It runs Phileas in-process, with a PhEye model for person names included in the Docker image. See the overview.

docs.title: Why should I use it?
docs.text: It puts redaction in the network path, where applications cannot skip it, and keeps a record of what was found in each request. It is designed to reduce how much sensitive data reaches LLM providers and to support your compliance efforts. Detection is probabilistic and does not catch every instance, so validate the output against your own data.

docs.title: Which AI providers are supported?
docs.text:
• OpenAI
  • Azure OpenAI
  • Anthropic (Claude)
  • Google Gemini
  • Google Vertex AI
  • Ollama
  • Amazon Bedrock (Converse and ConverseStream for any model; InvokeModel for Anthropic Claude and Amazon Titan and Cohere embedding models)
  • OpenAI-compatible providers (Mistral, vLLM, LM Studio, and others) configured under proxy.providers.openai-compatible

Streaming and non-streaming requests are supported for all of them. See Usage.

docs.title: Do I need a Philter instance?
docs.text: No. Since version 1.0 the proxy redacts in-process with Phileas, the library under Philter, and needs no other service. Earlier versions (0.x) sent each text to a Philter instance. Policies are the same format in both, so a Philter policy works in the proxy, except that the proxy refuses a policy that names a PhEye endpoint, generators, or files and environment variables the deployment has not allowed. See Policies.

docs.title: Does it support streaming?
docs.text: Yes, for every provider. Without response scanning, streamed responses are forwarded as they arrive. With response scanning, the proxy scans the stream as it arrives, holding back a little text so a value split across fragments is scanned whole. See Streamed responses.

docs.title: Can the proxy scan LLM responses for PII, not just requests?
docs.text: Yes, turned on per route. It can redact what it finds, block the response, or return it unchanged and record what it found. See Response Scanning.

docs.title: Does response scanning add latency?
docs.text: Yes. A normal response is scanned after it arrives, which adds about the time it took to redact the request. A streamed response reaches the client a little later than it arrives, since text is held back until it can be scanned. Turn scanning on only for the routes that need it. See Load tests.

docs.title: Can it redact file uploads, audio, or images?
docs.text:
No. The proxy handles text conversations only. It expects a JSON request body and rejects multipart/form-data with 400 invalid_request / unsupported_content_type, so file uploads (/v1/files), audio transcriptions (/v1/audio/transcriptions), and image edits and variations are not proxied. Route those calls directly to the provider.

The proxy does not parse multipart bodies, so image edits and file uploads will not be supported. Audio is the exception and is tracked in #40: its body is binary with no inbound text, so it can be forwarded untouched and the transcript scanned on the way back. See Supported request types.

The proxy redacts text only, and does not inspect what an image, recording, video, or file contains. By default it refuses a JSON request that carries one, such as an image_url or input_audio content part, with 400 invalid_request / media_not_allowed. Set media: forward on a route (or in proxy.defaults) to forward those requests with the media unchanged and unredacted. Images and audio in responses are returned unscanned. Remove or redact media before the request reaches the proxy if it can contain sensitive data. See Images, audio, and files are not redacted.

docs.title: Is any sensitive data logged?
docs.text:
The audit log holds metadata only: provider, model, policy, counts of what was found by type, status, and timing. It never holds the text of a prompt or response. It does hold the client's IP address, which may be personal data under GDPR. Metric labels hold no text either.

What the proxy does store is in its database: the policies, encrypted with the encryption key; hashed API keys; the audit log; and, for contexts, each replacement, encrypted, with a keyed hash of the original value it replaces (the original itself is not stored).

docs.title: How do I configure the proxy?
docs.text: With application.yaml and environment variables. See Configuration.

docs.title: Does the proxy support authentication?
docs.text: Yes, always. Every request to a provider needs a proxy key in x-philter-proxy-key, and the admin API needs a key with the admin role. Keys can be limited to providers, models, and paths, and bound to a policy. See API keys. Mutual TLS is available too; see Certificates. Authentication covers proxy keys and which provider credentials are passed through.

docs.title: Does the proxy hold my provider API keys?
docs.text: No, except for the providers it authenticates to itself. For OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible providers, and Azure with an API key, the client sends its own provider key, which the proxy forwards unchanged. For Azure with Entra ID, Vertex AI, and Bedrock, the proxy uses one credential configured for the deployment. A proxy key never maps to a provider key; see Authentication.

docs.title: Are API keys hashed at rest?
docs.text: Yes. Keys are 32 random bytes, and only their SHA-256 hashes are stored. A key is shown once, when it is created.

docs.title: Can I run more than one instance?
docs.text: Each instance needs its own database. The proxy keeps its policies, keys, contexts, and audit log in a SQLite file, and refuses to start on a file another instance is using. For more capacity, give the instance more CPU, or run several instances, each with its own database and keys, behind your gateway.

docs.title: What endpoints should I use for health checks?
docs.text: /livez for liveness and /readyz for readiness. /readyz answers once the proxy has finished loading the configured policies and their models; a policy that cannot be loaded is logged rather than holding readiness back. See Health endpoints.

docs.title: Does the proxy support OpenTelemetry tracing?
docs.text: Yes. Traces are exported over OTLP once you set an endpoint; nothing is exported by default. Each sampled request's trace ID is recorded in its audit entry either way. See Distributed Tracing.

docs.title: Where can I see throughput and latency numbers?
docs.text: See Load tests for a reference baseline and how to reproduce it.

docs.title: Can I use the proxy with Mistral, vLLM, or other OpenAI-compatible providers?
docs.text: Yes. Add each under proxy.providers.openai-compatible and call it at /<name>/v1/.... See OpenAI-compatible providers.

docs.title: How does Bedrock authentication work?
docs.text: The proxy signs each request with SigV4 using its own AWS credentials, from the AWS default chain, optionally assuming a role. Clients send no AWS credentials. See Amazon Bedrock.

docs.title: Does the proxy support streaming with Amazon Bedrock?
docs.text: Yes. /model/<model>/converse-stream responses, and /model/<model>/invoke-with-response-stream responses from Claude models, are forwarded, or scanned with response scanning on, in AWS's event stream format.

docs.title: Can I bound how many requests the proxy handles at once?
docs.text: Yes, with proxy.limits.max-concurrent-requests, which is 200 by default. When the limit is reached, the proxy answers 503 with Retry-After: 1 instead of queuing the request. Per-client limits belong to your AI gateway.

docs.title: What format are the proxy's error responses in?
docs.text:
{"error":{"message":"...","type":"...","code":"...","request_id":"..."}}

type and code are stable. Every response carries an X-Request-Id header, and the audit entry for the request records the same ID and the error's type and code. Errors from the provider are returned unchanged, in the provider's format. See Errors.

docs.title: Can I cap token spend, cache responses, or rate limit?
docs.text: No. Those belong to an AI gateway, which the proxy is designed to run alongside. The proxy does not track token usage at all. See Using with an AI Gateway.

docs.title: Can the proxy restore the original values in a response?
docs.text: No. A response comes back with the replacements in it. Re-identification of values encrypted with CRYPTO_REPLACE is tracked in #21.

docs.title: Is the proxy open source?
docs.text: Yes, under the Apache License 2.0. The source is at github.com/philterd/philter-ai-proxy.

docs.title: Is commercial support available?
docs.text: Yes, commercial support for Philter AI Proxy is available from Philterd. Please contact us for more information.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: The proxy ships as a Docker image, philterd/philter-ai-proxy, that includes the PhEye model the default policy uses to find person names. It also runs as a jar on Java 25.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• About 1.5 GiB of memory. The PhEye model is loaded into memory when the proxy starts.
  • A persistent directory for the proxy's SQLite database, which holds policies, API keys, contexts, and the audit log.
  • Network access to the LLM providers you use.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
Generate the two keys the proxy needs, and keep a copy of the encryption key: the database cannot be read without it, and the proxy refuses to start with a different one.

export ENCRYPTION_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
export BOOTSTRAP_API_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"

docker run -d --name philter-ai-proxy \
  -p 8080:8080 -p 127.0.0.1:9090:9090 \
  -v philter-ai-proxy-data:/var/lib/philter-ai-proxy \
  -e PHILTER_AI_PROXY_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$ENCRYPTION_KEY" \
  -e PHILTER_AI_PROXY_BOOTSTRAP_API_KEY="$BOOTSTRAP_API_KEY" \
  philterd/philter-ai-proxy:1.0.0
  • PHILTER_AI_PROXY_ENCRYPTION_KEY encrypts the policies and context replacements the database stores: 32 bytes as 64 hex characters or base64.
  • PHILTER_AI_PROXY_BOOTSTRAP_API_KEY becomes an admin key on first start, while no API key exists. It must be at least 32 characters.
  • Port 8080 serves provider traffic and the admin API. Port 9090 serves Prometheus metrics, unauthenticated; the examples publish it on the host's loopback address only. Keep it off the internet.

The proxy serves HTTPS with a self-signed certificate it generates at startup, so curl needs -k. See Certificates to use your own, or to serve plain HTTP behind a load balancer.

Wait until the proxy has loaded the model:

curl -k https://localhost:8080/readyz

{"status":"ok"}

docs.title: Create a key for your application
docs.text:
Applications authenticate to the proxy with a proxy key. Create one with the admin API, using the bootstrap key:

curl -k https://localhost:8080/admin/api/keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOOTSTRAP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "my-app", "roles": ["proxy"]}'

{"roles":["proxy"],"providers":[],"models":[],"paths":[],"id":"5f0c8a4e-...","name":"my-app","createdAt":"...","key":"pap_..."}

The key is shown only once. See API keys for limiting a key to providers, models, paths, or a policy.

docs.title: Send a request
docs.text:
Point the application at the proxy instead of the provider. It sends its provider credential as usual and its proxy key in x-philter-proxy-key:

curl -k https://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "x-philter-proxy-key: $PROXY_KEY" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "George Washington wrote to me at george@example.com."}]}'

OpenAI receives {{{REDACTED-name}}} wrote to me at {{{REDACTED-email-address}}}. The default policy finds person names, SSNs, and email addresses; see Policies to change it.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Settings come from application.yaml and environment variables; see Configuration. To use a settings file, mount it and point the proxy at it:

docker run -d --name philter-ai-proxy \
  -p 8080:8080 -p 127.0.0.1:9090:9090 \
  -v philter-ai-proxy-data:/var/lib/philter-ai-proxy \
  -v "$PWD/application.yaml:/etc/philter-ai-proxy/application.yaml:ro" \
  -e SPRING_CONFIG_ADDITIONAL_LOCATION=file:/etc/philter-ai-proxy/application.yaml \
  -e PHILTER_AI_PROXY_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$ENCRYPTION_KEY" \
  philterd/philter-ai-proxy:1.0.0

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
The repository's docker-compose.yaml builds the image from source and reads its settings from application.yaml and its keys from .env:

cp .env.example .env     # then set both keys in .env
docker compose up -d --build

docs.title: Building from Source
docs.text:
The build needs Java 25. The Maven wrapper downloads Maven.

./mvnw package
java --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED -jar target/philter-ai-proxy.jar \
  --proxy.storage.sqlite-path=./data/philter-ai-proxy.db \
  --proxy.models.directory=./models \
  --proxy.security.encryption-key="$ENCRYPTION_KEY" \
  --proxy.security.bootstrap-api-key="$BOOTSTRAP_API_KEY"

The jar does not include the model. The default policy names ph-eye-pii-en-small, which it expects in <models directory>/ph-eye-pii-en-small: download gliner_config.json, tokenizer.json, and model.onnx from the onnx folder of philterd/ph-eye-pii-en-small into that directory, or change the default policy. Without the model, requests that use the default policy are refused with policy_invalid.

Run without a certificate setting, the jar serves plain HTTP. ./mvnw verify runs the tests and the coverage check.

docs.title: Checking the version
docs.text:
java -jar target/philter-ai-proxy.jar --version

philter-ai-proxy 1.0.0

docs.title: Validating the configuration
docs.text:
--validate-config checks the settings (providers, the encryption key, trusted proxies) and exits without serving requests. It does not open the database, so it can run beside a running proxy. It exits non-zero when the configuration is invalid.

docker run --rm -e PHILTER_AI_PROXY_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$ENCRYPTION_KEY" philterd/philter-ai-proxy:1.0.0 --validate-config

The configuration is valid.

docs.title: Certificates
docs.text:
The image serves HTTPS with a self-signed certificate generated at startup (PROXY_TLS_DEVSELFSIGNEDCERT=true). It encrypts the connection but does not prove the proxy's identity, so clients must skip verification. Use it for evaluation only.

To serve your own certificate, give it and its private key in PEM form:

docker run -d --name philter-ai-proxy \
  -p 8080:8080 -p 127.0.0.1:9090:9090 \
  -v philter-ai-proxy-data:/var/lib/philter-ai-proxy \
  -v "$PWD/tls:/etc/philter-ai-proxy/tls:ro" \
  -e SERVER_SSL_CERTIFICATE=/etc/philter-ai-proxy/tls/tls.crt \
  -e SERVER_SSL_CERTIFICATEPRIVATEKEY=/etc/philter-ai-proxy/tls/tls.key \
  -e SERVER_SSL_ENABLEDPROTOCOLS=TLSv1.3,TLSv1.2 \
  -e PHILTER_AI_PROXY_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$ENCRYPTION_KEY" \
  philterd/philter-ai-proxy:1.0.0

A configured certificate takes precedence over the self-signed one. To require client certificates (mutual TLS), also set SERVER_SSL_TRUSTCERTIFICATE to a PEM file of the CA that signs them and SERVER_SSL_CLIENTAUTH=need.

When a load balancer, ingress, or service mesh terminates TLS in front of the proxy, serve plain HTTP with PROXY_TLS_DEVSELFSIGNEDCERT=false.

The metrics port (9090) always serves plain HTTP.

docs.title: Load tests
docs.text: A k6 harness lives at test/load/ in the repository. It brings up a stub LLM provider and the proxy built from the repository, with the default policy and its bundled person-name model, and runs five scenarios: inbound redaction for OpenAI and Anthropic, a streamed response, response scanning, and a baseline that skips the proxy.

docs.title: Reference baseline
docs.text:
Measured on the reference instance below on 2026-11-02: 10 virtual users, 20 seconds per scenario, the same prompt in every request (The SSN on file is 123-45-6789. Summarize the case.). The default policy runs the PhEye model over every prompt, and a context is configured, so each request also reads and writes the SQLite context store.

Scenario Iterations req/s p50 (ms) p95 (ms) p99 (ms) Failures no-redaction (direct to the stub, no proxy) 741,701 37,084 0.2 0.4 0.6 0.000% openai (inbound redaction) 1,684 84 110.7 174.7 241.5 0.000% anthropic (inbound redaction) 1,746 87 104.9 170.4 270.1 0.000% openai-streaming (inbound redaction, streamed response passed through) 1,744 87 113.3 131.6 146.7 0.000% outbound-scan (inbound redaction and response scanning) 809 40 241.0 328.8 365.2 0.000%

Before 2026-11-02 the stub answered openai-streaming without streaming, since it streamed only for a ?stream=1 query parameter; it now streams when the body asks, as providers do. The earlier figures for the other scenarios were within a few percent of these.

docs.title: Reading the table
docs.text:
The no-redaction row is the baseline: k6 calls the stub directly. The difference between it and another row is the cost of the proxy for that flow.

  • The model sets the throughput. Running the PhEye person-name model on the CPU is most of each request's cost: about 110 ms at the median with 10 requests at a time, and about 85 requests a second on this machine. The rest of the proxy (authentication, routing, the context store, forwarding) is small beside it.
  • Response scanning redacts twice, the prompt and the response, so outbound-scan runs at about half the throughput.
  • Providers cost the same. OpenAI, Anthropic, and the streamed response run the same redaction, so their rows match.
  • A pattern-only policy is much faster. A policy without a PhEye filter (SSNs, email addresses, phone numbers, and the like) skips the model.

For more throughput, give the proxy more CPU, or run more instances, each with its own database, behind your gateway. The model can also run on a GPU through ONNX Runtime's GPU build; the image ships the CPU build.

docs.title: Reference instance
docs.text:
• CPU: Intel Core i5-11400 @ 2.60 GHz, 12 logical cores.
  • RAM: 62 GiB.
  • OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS.
  • Docker: Engine 29.9.2.
  • Network: every component on the same host, over the docker-compose network.

The stub, the proxy, and the k6 container ran on the same machine, so they competed for CPU.

docs.title: How to reproduce
docs.text:
# From the repository root.
docker compose -f test/load/docker-compose.load.yaml up -d --build
for s in no-redaction openai anthropic openai-streaming outbound-scan; do
  VUS=10 DURATION=20s ./test/load/run.sh "$s"
done
docker compose -f test/load/docker-compose.load.yaml down -v

run.sh waits until the proxy is ready, creates a proxy key with the admin API, and runs the scenario. Each scenario's summary is written to test/load/results/<scenario>.summary.json. If ports 8080, 9090, or 8090 are taken on your machine, set PROXY_PORT, METRICS_PORT, or STUB_PORT for docker compose, and PROXY_URL (such as https://localhost:18080) for run.sh.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: A scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/load-test.yml) runs the scenarios weekly and on workflow_dispatch, and uploads the summaries as artifacts. The table above is a point-in-time reference and is not updated by the workflow.

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text: The proxy exposes Prometheus metrics, health endpoints, an audit log, and optional OpenTelemetry traces. None of them carries the text of a prompt or response.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Metrics are served for Prometheus at /metrics on the management port, 9090 (management.server.port), always over plain HTTP. Keep the port off the internet.

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: philter-ai-proxy
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["philter-ai-proxy:9090"]
Metric Type Labels Meaning philter_proxy_requests_total counter provider, status, policy Requests handled, by the status returned to the client. philter_proxy_request_duration_seconds histogram provider Time to handle a request, including the provider's response. philter_proxy_redaction_duration_seconds histogram provider, policy Time spent redacting a request's text. philter_proxy_entities_redacted_total counter entity_type, provider Values found in requests, by filter type (for example ssn, email-address, name). philter_proxy_upstream_errors_total counter provider, status Provider responses with status 400 or above, and providers that could not be reached (502). philter_proxy_redaction_errors_total counter provider Requests refused, or streams ended, because redaction or scanning failed. philter_proxy_concurrency_shed_total counter Requests refused at proxy.limits.max-concurrent-requests. philter_proxy_active_requests gauge Requests in flight. philter_proxy_concurrency_limit gauge The configured concurrency limit; 0 is no limit.

A counter appears once it has first counted something. The JVM, HTTP server, and process metrics that Spring Boot provides are served too.

docs.title: Health endpoints
docs.text:
All three are served on port 8080 without authentication.

Endpoint Answers 200 Use it for /livez While the process runs The liveness probe. /readyz Once the proxy has finished loading the policies the configuration names (the default and each route's) and their models, and while the database is usable; 503 otherwise The readiness probe. Loading the bundled model takes several seconds after start. A policy that cannot be loaded, such as one whose model is missing, is logged and does not hold readiness back; requests that use it are refused with policy_invalid. /health While the database is usable; 503 otherwise Monitoring. It answers with the standard Philterd health response, {"status": "UP", "applicationVersion": "1.0.0"}.

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text:
Each request to a provider produces one audit entry, written:

  • to the proxy's database, in the audit_log table;
  • to standard output as one JSON line, through the philter-ai-proxy.audit logger;
  • and to proxy.audit.file when it is set, as one JSON line, in a file created readable only by the proxy's user.

The database copy is kept until proxy.audit.retention-days removes it (off by default). The model field holds at most 256 characters of what the client sent.

{"timestamp":"2026-11-01T14:02:11.482Z","request_id":"6f1c...","event":"proxy_request","provider":"openai","model":"gpt-4o-mini","policy_name":"default","key_id":"5f0c8a4e-...","trace_id":"4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736","client_ip":"203.0.113.50","http_status":200,"fields_redacted":1,"entity_count":2,"entity_types":{"email-address":1,"name":1},"redact_latency_ms":31,"duration_ms":842,"streamed":false}
Field Meaning request_id The X-Request-Id returned to the client. provider, model, policy_name, context What the request used. key_id The ID of the proxy key, never the key. trace_id The OpenTelemetry trace ID, when the request was sampled. Recorded whether or not traces are exported. A client that sends a W3C traceparent header continues its own trace, so the client chooses this ID; use it to correlate, not as evidence. client_ip The client's address; see proxy.security.trusted-proxies. http_status The status returned to the client. fields_redacted, entity_count, entity_types How many text fields had values replaced, and how many values of each type were found in the request. outbound_action, outbound_entity_count, outbound_entity_types With response scanning: the action, and what was found in the response. redact_latency_ms, duration_ms Time spent redacting the request, and handling it in all. streamed Whether the response was a stream. error_type, error_code For a refused or failed request, the error the client received.

The admin API records its changes too: policy_created, policy_replaced, policy_deleted, api_key_created, and api_key_deleted, each with the acting key's ID.

docs.title: Distributed Tracing
docs.text:
The proxy can export OpenTelemetry traces over OTLP. Nothing is exported by default; setting an OTLP endpoint turns export on.

management:
  opentelemetry:
    tracing:
      export:
        otlp:
          endpoint: http://otel-collector:4318/v1/traces

Or with an environment variable: MANAGEMENT_OPENTELEMETRY_TRACING_EXPORT_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4318/v1/traces. management.tracing.export.enabled: false stops export while leaving the endpoint set.

Every request is sampled by default (management.tracing.sampling.probability: 1.0); lower it for busy deployments. The service name is philter-ai-proxy. Each sampled request's trace ID is recorded in its audit entry as trace_id, whether or not traces are exported, so an audit entry can be found from a trace and the other way around.

docs.title: Grafana Dashboard
docs.text: A dashboard for these metrics is at deploy/grafana/philter-ai-proxy.json. Import it with Grafana's Dashboards, New, Import, and choose the Prometheus data source that scrapes the proxy. Its datasource variable lets the same JSON work across environments.

docs.title: Alerting rules
docs.text:
groups:
  - name: philter-ai-proxy
    rules:
      # Traffic flowing, 200s returning, and nothing being redacted. `or vector(0)` is needed because the
      # counter has no series until the first value is found.
      - alert: RedactionDetectionStopped
        expr: |
          (sum(rate(philter_proxy_entities_redacted_total[30m])) or vector(0)) == 0
          and sum(rate(philter_proxy_requests_total[30m])) > 0
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "The proxy is serving traffic but has found nothing to redact for 30 minutes"
          description: "Check that the policy in use matches the traffic and that the models it names are installed."

      - alert: RedactionErrors
        expr: rate(philter_proxy_redaction_errors_total[5m]) > 0
        for: 1m
        labels:
          severity: critical
        annotations:
          summary: "Requests are being refused because redaction failed"

      - alert: HighUpstreamErrorRate
        expr: |
          sum(rate(philter_proxy_upstream_errors_total[5m])) /
          sum(rate(philter_proxy_requests_total[5m])) > 0.05
        for: 2m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "More than 5% of provider requests are failing"

      - alert: HighRedactionLatency
        expr: |
          histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(philter_proxy_redaction_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))) > 1
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "Redaction p95 latency exceeds 1 second"

      - alert: ConcurrencyLimitShedding
        expr: rate(philter_proxy_concurrency_shed_total[5m]) > 0
        for: 2m
        labels:
